posts.title: finally started the game engine project!
posts.article:
hello again!


it's been pretty fun restarting this project again, but i'm doing it mainly because i have a completed vision (almost) for how it's gonna work.

in this post, i'm talking about BigEngine, my newish/oldish game engine.
new because it's now in proper development, and old because i had this idea maybe a year ago, and i came up with some prototypes using OpenGL and C#, which i was very much not skilled enough to do yet lol.
i recently came across this great library called raylib, which you can think of like a wrapper for OpenGL and GLAD that removes a lot of the weird useless boilerplate at it's core, it's fantastic.

well anyway, the goal with this project has always been to allow less experienced game developers to enter game dev without an airplane cockpit in front of them.
in other words, i want it to have a nice balance between being as simple as possible, but also as powerful as possible, and i feel like using raylib is the perfect choice for something like that, and i hope you'd agree.
if you'd like to give it a shot, it's not currently ready as of writing this, as i've just created the first major commit, but if you're in the future (and it's finished,) you can check it out here.

development screenshots




there are only 2 screenshots at the moment, because it is almost 2 am and i'm tired and that's all i've got done today lol.

i appreciate you being here.

have a good one :)

posts.title: public resource for liminal spaces
posts.article:
whats up.

an actual useful resource for once!

not long ago, i decided to spend 3 hours straight compiling 317 liminal space photos that made me say "ew". i couldn't tell you why it had to be the day i did it on, nor could i tell you why there are exactly 317, but who knows, maybe i'll maintain the list and add more photos in the future.

the full list of images are currently public on google drive here.

feel free to refer to this list for your own work, but be aware that i do not own any of these photos, so i don't recommend using any of them in anything other than personal use. i'm definitely not a lawyer, so you may not be able to use them in anything at all, for all i know.

i mainly compiled these together to use as reference for environments and set pieces for my games. the plan is to try and replicate the emotions i feel from the thought of what it would be like if i was in these situations, and to ask myself questions like "what would i do?", "where would i go?", "who would i talk to, if anyone else is there?", and "what could be beyond what i can't see from here?", and especially for that last one, i could figure out an answer just by looking through this list.

a lot of these images remind me of things i've been absolutely fascinated with recently, such as the environments from the half life series, primarily half life 2 and it's episodes, as well as half life alyx, which are both fantastic games with great environments and storytelling.
there's also some real gems from the gmod mapping community, they make some fantastic stuff too. if you're interested in these images and would like to see more content like them, you should definitely check out some of the exploration maps gmod map designers come up with, their work is astounding!

on that note, a youtuber named The Librarian is one who often delves into these maps in VR, and his commentary is enlightening in a few ways, it brings out some smaller details most wouldn't bother to really notice.
his videos of other games are also just lovely, i just couldn't recommend him enough.

anyway, regarding proper liminal spaces, you really have to be in it for the long run, and take everything in as best you can to allow them to really do their job. they're not really gonna truly work the way they're designed to if all you do is speed through them with 5 or 6 different peter griffin nextbots behind you.

and that's the tricky thing about making a game revolving around or taking place inside liminal spaces: you really need to encourage players to find themselves in these environments you build, to have it consistently emit the atmosphere you want, and that's exactly what my personal goal is: to get the player as grounded into my world as possible so that i can tell my stories with a maximum punch, so i believe that this list will be a massive help in doing that, and i think it could help you too, even outside of just that use case.
